response.passage: At the Zenith Robotics Club in Bengaluru, students are preparing for the annual Tech-Fest held on 15th March. Last year, the club members built 12 small robots to navigate a maze. This year, the club president, Rohan, decided to focus on drones. The drones are faster because they use lightweight carbon fiber frames. Rohan explains that the lightweight material allows the motors to spin at higher speeds without overheating. However, some students like Meera prefer the older robots because they are easier to repair. Meera spent 4 hours fixing a broken sensor on a robot yesterday. The club mentor, Mr. Sharma, says that the shift to drones is necessary to keep up with modern technology. He believes that learning about aerodynamics will help students understand how birds fly. While the club is busy, the nearby library remains quiet. The club members must finish their projects before the deadline to ensure they can participate in the competition. If they fail to complete the drones, they will not be allowed to enter the arena. The excitement in the room is high as everyone works together to solve complex coding problems.
response.summary: The Zenith Robotics Club is shifting from building robots to drones for an upcoming competition. Students and mentors are working hard to complete their projects before the deadline. The new drones are designed to be faster and more efficient than previous models.
